task: lifecycle-registry.ts LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS carries gates/effects/oracleRows/rendererRow per transition and phase-flow.ts/context.ts derive the phase graph from it, but the registry has no phase-to-commands or phase/transition-to-artifacts dimension. Command legality lives in command-policy.ts allowedPhases + config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS, artifact production lives implicitly across handlers, with no mechanical proof these stay consistent with the registry.
outcome: A framework maintainer runs the lifecycle registry consistency contract test (e.g. npm --prefix packages/main run test:lifecycle-registry-contract or an extension of an existing contract test) and sees output like 'lifecycle-registry consistency: PASS — command-policy/DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS/process-fact lifecycle all consistent with registry, 0 divergences'. If a maintainer later adds a command to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS without registering it in the registry command dimension, the contract test fails naming the divergent command. phase-flow.ts/context.ts derived values (phase ordinals, allowed transitions) are byte-identical before and after — no public behavior change.
facts: lifecycle-registry.ts LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS has gates/effects/oracleRows/rendererRow per transition (B-d339)
phase-flow.ts and context.ts already derive phase order + transition graph from lifecycle-registry
command-policy.ts CommandPolicy.allowedPhases declares per-command phase legality (85 entries)
config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS is a phase-to-commands map with a * wildcard bucket
process-fact-levels.ts / process-fact-registry.ts hold process facts including lifecycle gate rows
constraints: Additive only — no public behavior change, no TEST semantics change, no legacy main-type change, no story_advance restructure (Story 2/3/4 scope)
New registry dimensions (commands, artifacts) are read-only projections mirroring the existing lifecycleForwardTransitionsByPhase pattern
The consistency contract must FAIL on divergence and name the divergent command/artifact — not just warn
phase-flow.ts and context.ts must keep deriving from the registry; derived values must be byte-identical before/after
Handler 编码约定 not directly relevant (no new handler) but registry projection helpers must be pure functions
